title: MarshalEnvelope
description: The one response envelope every marshal command emits (AD-14, AD-39): {schema_version, command, status, verdict, data, data_version, findings, assumptions}. status is a pure function of verdict (status_for) and is never set independently -- the top-level oneOf encodes that partition so a wire-side validator rejects a mismatched pair, not just the producer's Envelope.__post_init__. additionalProperties is false at both the envelope and finding level -- an unrecognized/typo'd key is a schema violation; a genuinely new field is an envelope-schema change (AD-14), not a silent addition. 'data' stays open (type: object with no declared properties) since its shape is per-command and opaque to this envelope.

oneOf.description: AD-39: status 'ok' pairs only with verdicts {clean, warn}.
AD-39: status 'error' pairs only with verdicts {unevaluable, scope-violation, gate-failed, error}.

schema_version.description: Envelope schema version; bumps on ANY change to the envelope's key set -- additionalProperties is false, so even an additive key is a new schema version (a v1 validator would reject it), never a silent addition. const 1: this file IS the v1 schema -- a document claiming any other version must not validate against it.

command.description: The marshal command that produced this envelope -- never empty (matches Envelope.__post_init__'s non-empty check).

verdict.description: The closed 6-member lattice, strongest first: error > gate-failed > scope-violation > unevaluable > warn > clean (AD-7, AD-31).

data.description: Command-specific payload, opaque to this envelope.

data_version.description: The data payload's own version, from a registry, bumped independently of schema_version (AD-39).

code.description: Stable machine code from the central registry (AD-15, core/findings.py). [0-9] spelled explicitly so the pattern reads identically under ECMA-262 and Python re (Python's \d is Unicode-wide). The $(?!\n) tail closes Python's other divergence: re-based validators (python-jsonschema applies pattern via re.search) let $ match before a trailing newline, so without the lookahead 'MRS-GATE-001\n' would validate on the wire while the producer's fullmatch rejects it; under ECMA-262 the lookahead is inert ($ already means true end-of-string).

severity.description: Presentational only; the lattice member comes from verdict.classify(code) (AD-31).
